project.objective: When and where did Thomas Hanrahan, born about 1840 in Ireland and living in Saratoga, New York, in 1880, marry Johanna Ryan?

researcher_profile.narration_guidance: Plain language for someone who has never done genealogy. No identifiers, file names, tool names or field names. Never write GPS, proof, proved or exhaustive: say genealogy standards; call an answer a conclusion when it is well established and a finding otherwise; say what we searched and what we could not reach. Do not describe your own instructions or checks. Do not narrate between actions; report once when the step is done: what was found, in one paragraph, and what happens next in one sentence.

questions.question: When and where did Thomas Hanrahan, born about 1840 in Ireland and living in Saratoga, New York in 1880, marry Johanna Ryan?
questions.rationale: The objective is one event, the marriage, restated with identifying detail. The couple link rests on the 1880 census household and the children's records, which are sourced, so no premise needs verifying first. Three birth-place and birth-year disagreements among linked records are not yet registered as conflicts and may bear on the couple's identity later.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga, Saratoga, New York, United States
items.rationale: loc_001: the 1855 and 1865 New York State Census collections are name-searchable. The tree holds only the 1880 census (Thomas b. about 1840 Ireland, Johanna b. about 1845 Ireland, children recorded as New York-born, Mary about 15) and the Irish baptisms of Mary (1871) and John (1872, Ardfinnan); nothing shows where the couple lived before 1880. A 1865 household with Thomas, Johanna and a child would cap the marriage date and test the New York-birth claim. Search Hanrahan, Hanrehan, Hannahan, Hanraghan and Ryan, Ryon variants, and adjoining towns.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga, Saratoga, New York, United States
items.rationale: loc_001: the 1875 New York State Census is name-searchable and has a marriage and mortality schedule after each town's population schedule; browse it for a Hanrahan-Ryan marriage in 1874 in case the marriage was later than the 1880 census implies. The household also shows children's birthplaces, bearing on the Ireland-versus-New York conflicts.

United States Census 1860 and 1870 are name-searchable. The tree records Elizabeth b. about 1869 and Thomas b. about 1870 as born in New York City, so the 1870 household may be in New York City rather than Saratoga; Mary (about 1871) and John (1872) have Irish baptisms. Locating the couple in 1860 and 1870 shows where they were living and whether Johanna appears under Ryan or Hanrahan, directing the marriage search to the right place.

items.jurisdiction: New York, United States (including New York City)
items.rationale: loc_001: no reliable civil marriage record is likely for Saratoga 1848-1880, but the name-searchable New York Marriages 1686-1980, New York Church and Civil Marriages 1704-1995 and New York City Marriage Records 1829-1938 are cheap to search. NYC is included because two children are recorded as born there about 1869-1870. Accept a hit only if spouse names, ages and Irish birth fit; a name match alone does not identify this couple.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga County, New York (Catholic parishes, Diocese of Albany)
items.rationale: loc_001 names Catholic parish registers as the strongest lead but finds no Catholic register among its digitized volumes and the serving parish is unconfirmed. Search the name-searchable New York Church Records 1660-1954 and New York Church and Civil Marriages 1704-1995 first, then check volume_search results for full-text church marriage volumes, using the surname variants. The result may also identify the parish.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga and neighboring counties, New York (Catholic parishes)
items.rationale: Fallback for the previous item if FamilySearch yields nothing. Identify the Catholic parish serving Saratoga town via the Local Catholic Church research guide (freepages.rootsweb.com/~localcatholic/history/US-NewYorkNY.htm, per loc_001) and write to the Diocese of Albany archives; also check Findmypast's New York Roman Catholic Parish Marriages. Irish couples often married in the bride's parish, so include Albany, Washington, Rensselaer and Montgomery counties.

The name-searchable GenealogyBank Historic Newspaper Marriages 1815-2011 may carry a notice; loc_001 notes Ancestry's New York marriage newspaper extracts (Barber Collection, 1801-1880) as a subscription alternative. Notices can state the place and officiant, but Irish laborers' weddings were often not announced, so a miss is weak evidence.

items.jurisdiction: New York, United States (Saratoga and New York City)
items.rationale: FAN and indirect evidence: baptisms of the couple's children (Elizabeth about 1869 and Thomas about 1870 in New York City; any child born 1864-1868) in the name-searchable New York Births and Christenings 1640-1962 and New York Church Records 1660-1954 give parents' names, sometimes Johanna's maiden name and sponsors who may be Ryan or Hanrahan relatives. Sponsors and neighboring Ryan households in the 1865 census point to the bride's family and parish, where the marriage was most likely recorded. Corroboration only; a baptism does not prove the marriage date.

Naturalization (New York County Naturalization Records, Record of Naturalized Voters 1872-1878) and passenger lists (US Index to Passenger Arrivals 1820-1874) show when Thomas and Johanna arrived, which brackets whether the marriage could have occurred in New York or before emigration, relevant to the c_001/c_002 conflict between Irish baptisms in 1871-1872 and New York births claimed in 1880. Naturalization papers often state arrival year and birthplace.

Later records of the couple's own lives: New York State Death Index 1880-1956, New York Deaths and Burials, Cemetery Abstracts, and obituaries for Thomas and Johanna. Obituaries and burial records may give ages, birthplaces, years of marriage and the parish. Dates are sized to the couple's later lifespans, not the 1855-1870 marriage window.

log.notes: Census 1855-1865, Saratoga. 27 rows, Hanrahan/Hanna/Handron variants. Top ranked: 1860 US census Household of Margaret Hanrahan, Northumberland, Thomas b.1840 Ireland (MC4N-WKP), matchScore 0.33, attached to another person; outside the 1855-65 window. In that dwelling Thomas is listed with Margaret; family structure inferred from surname, ages and order, not stated, since 1860 has no relationship column. 1865 NY State census Northumberland, Thomas Hanrahan b.1843 (QVNN-7MNR), birthYearGap 3, no birthplace, needs-review; household contents not yet read. Other rows are surname-not-on-subject or birth-year conflicts (Handron, Hanna, Hannah, Hannen, Handen; Albany and Hadley households). 1855 NY census: no Hanrahan named Thomas in Saratoga. Collection mismatch noted: the 1860 row falls outside the requested range.

Top: MSG7-614 (Thomas Hanrahan, b. March 1843 Ireland; 1871 marriage event; Saratoga 1900 census) matchScore 0.46, birthYearConflict true, gap 3 from subject's about-1840 birth: needs-review, not adopted. Several NY Marriages index hits are father-of-bride/groom entries (not the subject). Result is a collection mismatch for the plan item's purpose; a collection-pinned follow-up is run next.

New York, Marriages, 1686-1980 pinned. 30 matches, none a groom named Thomas Hanrahan. Pool is fuzzy spellings (Hannan, Honan, Hannon) and Hanrahan/Thomas as father, father-in-law or mother-in-law on other couples' entries. Ranker: subject resolvable but no candidate scored above 0.01, a real negative for this query. Entries carrying Hannan/Honan/Hannon/Hanaman surnames are surnameNotOnSubject and not evidence for the subject. Nil for the subject as groom in this collection under this spelling; spelling variants not run here.

Spelling variant Hanrehan, same frame. 27 rows, same top set as log_004 (Hanrahan rows dominate the index; no Hanrehan-spelled Thomas in Saratoga). Top: 1865 NY State census Northumberland, Thomas Hanrahan b.1843 (QVNN-7MNR), now showing spouse Joanna Hanrahan; birthYearGap 3; needs-review. 1860 Margaret Hanrahan household (MC4N-WKP) outside the window; family structure there inferred from surname, ages and order. Non-Saratoga rows (Albany, Brooklyn) and surname-not-on-subject rows are not candidates for this subject.

Spouse-anchored search (spouse Johanna). 372 total, 50 returned, offset 0 only; the spouse anchor does not narrow to the couple. Candidate of interest: 1865 NY State census Northumberland, Thomas Hanrahan b.1843 (QVNN-7MNR), spouse present as Joanna Hanrahan (spelling differs from Johanna); a 1865 Northumberland household listing Mary Hanrahan b.1865 (QVNN-7MNY) is in the same dwelling; birthYearGap 3 keeps it needs-review. Other Hanrahan/Hanrihan/Handrahan couples (Albany, Waterford, Stillwater, Eliza/John Hanrahan in Northumberland) do not show a Thomas. Relative anchor is not confirmation; the spouse name is the only relative tied to this household in the rows returned.

1870 census, New York scope, surname Hanrahan, given name Thomas; 175 total, top 50 ranked against KHGX-XWG. Top rows: Thomas Hanrahan b.1840 Ireland, Buffalo, Erie (household of James Hanrahan; matchScore 0.19; attached to other tree person; no birth-year conflict). Thomas Hanrahan b.1838 Ireland, Brooklyn (household of Thomas Hanrahan, ark M8NR-MV6, same household as Thomas b.1869 New York, ark M8NR-MVF, gap 29 from subject); Thomas Hanrahan b.1841 Ireland, New York City (household of Mary Hanrahan, no surname-not-on-subject flag). Many rows carry birthYearConflict or surnameNotOnSubject (Hannon, Hanna, Hannan) and are not this surname; these are needs-review and not matches. Census 1870 collection 1438024 has no relationship-to-head column; household structure inferred. No row ties this person to spouse Johanna or the NYC address; identity unconfirmed.

1860 census, New York scope, surname Hanrahan, given name Thomas; 63 total, top 50 ranked against KHGX-XWG. Top match: Thomas Hanrahan b.1840 Ireland, Northumberland, Saratoga County (household of Margaret Hanrahan; matchScore 0.33; birth year matches subject; attached to other tree person; no conflict flag). 1860 census collection 1473181 has no relationship column; household structure inferred from surname, age and order. Other Hanrahan rows: Thomas b.1828 Ireland, Buffalo (gap -12), Thomas b.1851 and b.1821 New York City (gap 11 and -19), Thomas b.1860 Albany (gap 20). Remaining rows are Hannon, Hanna, Hannan, Handrahan, Hanrihan variants with surnameNotOnSubject or birth conflicts. The Saratoga match is consistent with the plan's Saratoga anchor but is unconfirmed.

New York City Marriage Records 1829-1938 pinned. 75 matches; top 50 read, the last 25 not paged. No groom named Thomas Hanrahan in the 50 read. Only Hanrahan-surnamed Thomas entries are fathers of bride or of groom on other couples' entries, not the subject. Nearest groom: Thomas L Hanna, b. 1843 Staten Island, married 28 Jan 1869 Manhattan (Sarah Grace Byers); and Thomas Hanna / Thomas Hannon (1837 Ireland, married 1863). Both fail on surname (Hanna, Hannon) and birthplace, and Hanna is US-born, so not the subject; no surname tie to the subject exists in the project. Ranker: no candidate scored above 0.01. Remaining 25 unread results would need paging before a full negative. Irish-born, marriage-year fit not established.

Read of the 1865 NY State census, Northumberland, Saratoga (QVNN-7MNR). Household as indexed: Thomas Hanrahan b.1843 (indexed birth range 1842-43; no birthplace), Joanna Hanrahan b.1846 (spelling differs from tree's Johanna), Mary Hanrahan b.1865 (fits tree's Mary about 15 in 1880). Also indexed in the dwelling: Paines Durkins b.1842, Ellen Durkins b.1842, Anna Mary Durkins b.1865; the index draws parent-child links from Thomas and Joanna to Anna Mary Durkins, an indexer inference, not a stated relationship. 1865 schedule has no relationship-to-head column in this read, so family structure is inferred from surnames and order. Birth-year gap 3 from the tree's about 1840; birthplace not recorded; the index flags a birth-year conflict. Status: needs-review. Possible namesake: Thomas Hanrahan b.1840 Ireland in the 1860 Northumberland household of Margaret Hanrahan (MC4N-WKP) is in the same town and not yet tied to this 1865 household. Ryan/Ryon variants not yet searched.

Top-ranked hit is 1900 US Census household of Thomas Hanrahan (birth March 1843, Ireland; immigration 1860; marriage 1871; Saratoga city), matchScore 0.46, birthYearGap 3 against subject's about 1840, not a church record; treat as needs-review. 1900 census lists no relationships; family structure inferred only. Collection mismatch again: church filter returned Find a Grave, NY State Death Index, BillionGraves, NYC marriages. No church register row. Ranker: no subject-scoring candidate.

2087 matches; 50 ranked. No candidate is confirmed as the subject. Cross-check of top rows against subject (Thomas Hanrahan, b. about 1840, Ireland): (1) 27R2-GPJ, Thos Hanrahan, b.1839 Ireland, NY County passenger arrival 1857, no birth-year conflict, needs-review (arrival 1857 sits oddly with Irish baptisms 1871-72; no spouse/child anchor). (2) QV33-FS7J Thomas b.1837 Ireland, arrival 1863, gap -3, flagged birthYearConflict, needs-review. (3) KDF9-2DR Thos b.1842 UK, Famine Irish index 1851 as a child, gap +2, birthplace UK not Ireland, needs-review. (4) 27RF-XCF Thos b.1841 England, arrival 1856, birthplace England, needs-review. Other rows fall outside +/-5 years or flagged. Naturalization index rows (1859-1880, county and Soundex collections) carry no birth date and cannot be triaged on age; several list birthplace Ireland or England. Subject has no spouse anchor in this search, so Johanna is not used to resolve identity. Passenger/naturalization arrival years are not extracted here. Result set is a 2087-match pool; only the top 50 by rank were read. Four earlier staged searches (results/.staging/0ad2a9fa..., 5a485c4b..., cd0bdeeb..., 86a742b3...) were found unlogged in the staging area; they were not run by this invocation and are not logged here.

Given-name and spouse variant search (Thomas / spouse Johanna) with Saratoga marriage scope. No church or marriage register for the couple returned. Top rows are census households: 1880 census Thomas Hanrahan, b. 1840 Ireland, stone mason, Saratoga city, spouse Johannah, attachedToSubject true, matchScore 0.63, birth year gap 0 against 'about 1840' (strongest fit so far, but 1880 schedule has no relationship column; spouse inferred from the listing). 1900 census Thomas b. March 1843 Ireland, marriage 1871, Saratoga, matchScore 0.46, birth year gap 3, not attached, needs-review. Other rows are NY state census, land assessments, death indexes, and Albany/Kings/Minnesota Thomas Hanrahans not matching the couple. Surname-not-on-subject rows (Hannan, Hannin) excluded.

Broad surname search, no given name or parent anchor. 34,351 hits, 50 returned and ranked against subject KHGX-XWG. No candidate scored above 0.01; ranker reports a real negative for this pool. Top-ranked rows are other Hanrahans (John 1838 Ireland d.1868 Manhattan; Henry Albany; Frank/Patrick F burials 1870) with no link to Thomas or to a baptism of his children. Cross-check: none of the top rows is a baptism of a child of Thomas and Johanna. Several rows carry surnames not on the subject (Handraen, Hannan, Hannon), flagged surnameNotOnSubject. Index does not return the couple's children under this query.

Parent-anchored retry: father Thomas, mother Johanna. 29,877 hits, 50 returned and ranked against subject. No candidate scored above 0.01; ranker reports a real negative. relativeTerms: 15 of 50 name no father and 15 name no mother, so those are consistent with the anchor, not evidence for it. Only parent-naming hits in this pool that touch the family are a Hanrahan born 18 May 1866 Manhattan (mother Johanna Hanrahan, father present but unnamed) and a 1866 marriage of Margaret Hanrahan whose father is Thos. Hanrahan and mother Johanna Hanley. Neither is linked to the subject, neither names the subject as father, and neither is adopted here; both are needs-review pending an anchor (a baptism naming Thomas Hanrahan as father, or a marriage record for Thomas). childrenSearch flag: this search was held to anyPlace; a no-place, recordCountry-anchored children search is still to be run before reporting children.

Ranked top 50 of 1089 matches. No match confirmed for Thomas Hanrahan (about 1840, Ireland) in Saratoga County. Saratoga-area candidates: Thomas Hanrahan d. 25 Feb 1914 Schuylerville (state death index QGPB-5Q3N, no birth date; Find a Grave QK1X-T6QN, birth 1845, gap 5, birthYearConflict flagged), needs-review; Thomas F Hanrahan d. 1 Apr 1902 Schuylerville (QGKC-FLKH, no birth date, attached to other), needs-review; Thomas Hanrahan d. 19 May 1900 Waterford burial (W6PP-ZJZM, no birth date), and d. 19 May 1900 Cohoes (QG6H-SH3C), same date, different place, undetermined. A narrower Saratoga-only cemetery search is still needed.

Unfiltered full-text search, Keywords only, facets requested. 1,453 hits; top 5 examined. All five are Irish legal deeds and wills (1912-1925) with Hanrahan and Ryan among many names; none is a marriage notice and none names a Saratoga or New York couple. Not a newspaper search on its own; read as a corpus-wide pass.

Unfiltered Keywords search, spouse given-name variant Johanna. 900 hits; top 5 examined. Results are a Montana/Texas family memoir, an Irish 1901 census, an Irish will, a Suffolk NY citizenship record and a Michigan death register. None is a marriage notice for Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan. Spelling variants Johannah, Joanna not run.

Exact-name phrase pass with both full names together, no filters. Four hits. Two Limerick County, Ireland court registers 1863-1866 list a Thomas Hanrahan and a Johanna Ryan on the same page (no link to the subject shown, Limerick is not Saratoga). A Torrington, Connecticut civil marriage and birth register from 1892 lists Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan on one page, outside the 1855-1872 window and in a different state; not adopted without a check of the entries. Doubtful for the subject; do not extract as the marriage.

Top match MSG7-614 (Thomas Hanrahan, Saratoga city, married, born March 1843 Ireland, immigration 1860, marriage 1871): matchScore 0.85, birthYearConflict true, gap 3 years against subject birth about 1840, not attached to subject. Needs-review per birth-year conflict; read before any use. Other rows are different surnames or other places (Hannan, Hanahan in Stillwater, Hanrahan in Albany and Watervliet), none a confirmed candidate.

Secondary 1910 census check. Collection 1727033 (US Census 1910). Ranking reports no candidate above 0.01 (subjectResolvable false, read as a real negative for this query). Only Saratoga-county row near the subject is Thomas Hanahan, Saratoga, born 1838 Ireland, widowed, immigration 1888 (ark M5SP-CC4), spelled Hanahan; the 1888 immigration year conflicts with the 1860 year on the 1900 candidate, so it is not treated as the same person without an anchor. # Locality Guide: Saratoga, Saratoga County, New York (1855-1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** February 7, 1791, from Albany County
- **County seat:** Ballston Spa
- **Parent jurisdiction:** New York
- **Population during period:** 45,646 (1850); 51,729 (1860); 51,529 (1870, a slight decline); 55,156 (1880), per the county's FamilySearch Wiki page
- **Economy:** Saratoga Springs' mineral-spring resort economy drew visitors and workers; the Hudson River/Champlain Canal corridor supported milling, quarrying and transportation trades — consistent with a stone mason's work
- **Ethnic composition:** The FamilySearch Wiki does not break out ethnic composition for this county; an Irish Catholic immigrant community is attested by the subject family's own presence in Saratoga by 1880
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist, Reformed Protestant Dutch, Presbyterian, Society of Friends (Quaker) congregations are documented from the 1700s-1800s (NYGenWeb/FamilySearch Wiki); Catholic parishes in the county fall under the Diocese of Albany, but no specific parish serving the town of Saratoga in this period was named by any tool result
- **Key historical events:** None specific to 1855-1880 named by the FamilySearch Wiki beyond the county's formation and ordinary 19th-century growth

## Boundary changes
- Saratoga County was created from Albany County on February 7, 1791, and its boundaries were stable through 1855-1880 — no further splits or annexations are noted on its FamilySearch Wiki page.
- Neighboring counties, per the same page: Albany, Fulton, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Warren, Washington. A family near the county line could have records in any of these, especially Washington or Albany County.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Marriages were first recorded locally (town/village/city) starting 1847, but compliance lapsed within a few years; statewide registration of births, marriages, and deaths began in 1880-1881, with compliance incomplete until 1913 (births) and 1890 (deaths) — [New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records). The county's own page gives 1880 for both birth and death registration, and 1908 for marriage, likely referring to when county-level marriage license records at the Clerk's office became reliably complete — [Saratoga County, New York Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy).
- **What exists:** No dedicated civil marriage register is likely to survive for an 1855-1879 Saratoga marriage given the above. "New York, Marriages, 1686-1980" (FamilySearch collection 1680847, index only) and "New York, County Marriages, 1778-1848; 1908-1937" (collection 1618491) bracket but do not cover 1848-1907 county civil marriages well.
- **Where held:** Town/village/city clerks for any local records that do survive; Saratoga County Clerk's office for marriage, divorce, court and land records from 1791 forward; New York State Department of Health for anything recorded after 1880.
- **Gaps:** No systematic civil marriage record exists for this county 1848-1880 — this is the central obstacle to finding the Hanrahan-Ryan marriage through vital records.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic (or other) church marriage registers are the primary alternative; newspaper marriage notices; the 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage/mortality schedules (12 months before the census).

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Episcopal, Methodist, Reformed Protestant Dutch, Society of Friends (1700s-1800s, per NYGenWeb/wiki); Catholic parishes under the Diocese of Albany.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials; Quaker Saratoga Monthly Meeting minutes (1794-1862, FS Library film 17403).
- **Where held:** No tool result named the specific Catholic parish serving the town of Saratoga/Schuylerville in 1855-1880; the Diocese of Albany holds parish sacramental registers for the diocese generally. The [Local Catholic Church and Family History & Genealogical Research Guide](https://freepages.rootsweb.com/~localcatholic/history/US-NewYorkNY.htm) identifies Saratoga County's parishes and their founding years and is the recommended starting point. Non-Catholic registers located by volume_search: Schuylerville Reformed Dutch Protestant Church marriages 1790-1857 (image group 007767898_009_M98S-6Q6, 52% indexed, full-text searchable); First Presbyterian Church at Ballston Center marriages 1783-1865 (007767898_011_M98S-6QF, 52% indexed); Presbyterian Church, Charlton, marriages 1801-1862 (007767898_012_M98S-6QN, 51% indexed) and births/christenings 1801-1855 (007767897_006_M94S-YWH, browse-only, 0% indexed); Reformed Dutch Church of Amity, Vischer Ferry, marriages 1840-1855 (007767898_017_M98S-6QL, 34% indexed).
- **Gaps:** No Catholic parish register for this county and period was found by any tool in this survey — a coverage gap in both the FamilySearch Wiki and FamilySearch's digitized volumes; the researcher must identify and contact the specific parish directly.
- **Language:** English for the denominations found; Catholic registers in this period are commonly in Latin, but this was not confirmed for any specific Saratoga County parish.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** 1850, 1860, 1870, 1880 federal censuses cover this period (standard national schedule; mortality schedules for 1850-1880 also exist, per Ancestry link in the wiki page, also on FS Library Films 1415128-42).
- **State/provincial census:** New York State Census for 1855, 1865, and 1875 — all three are digitized with index & images on FamilySearch (collections 1937366, 1491284, 1918735 respectively) and also at Ancestry ($). The 1865 and 1875 state censuses carry marriage and mortality schedules for the 12 months before the census, appended after the population schedule for each town.
- **Other enumerations:** None specific to Saratoga County beyond the above was found.
- **Access:** State and federal census years above are indexed with images on FamilySearch; always check adjoining towns in case of a mid-decade move.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, petitions, inventories.
- **Testate or intestate:** Unknown for Thomas Hanrahan or Johanna Ryan at this stage; search both wills and administration indexes.
- **Date range:** From county formation (1791) forward, per the Surrogate Court.
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Surrogate Court; FamilySearch has "New York Probate Records, 1629-1971" (collection 1920234, images only) and FS Library Film 555744/555745 cover wills/administrations 1791-1921 for the county, per volume_search and catalog_search results. Abstracts of early wills and surrogate records (1791-1815) were also catalogued (koha:453453, koha:149586).

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not detailed by any tool result for this county.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** County Clerk's office, per the county genealogy page; no separate state land office role was named for this period.
- **Types:** Deeds, grants, mortgages; "New York, Land Records, 1630-1975" (FamilySearch collection 2078654, index & images) covers the state broadly.
- **Date range:** From 1791 (county formation).
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Clerk's office (per the county's courthouse entry); FamilySearch catalog volumes for Saratoga land records (77 volumes matched in volume_search for this period, mostly full-text searchable).

### Military records

## Research tips
- Civil marriage registration did not reliably exist in New York State until 1880, with compliance incomplete even then — [New York Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records) — so a Catholic parish marriage register is the most promising lead for an 1855-1879 Hanrahan-Ryan marriage, not a civil record search.
- Always search both the town of Saratoga's own records and the neighboring counties — Albany, Fulton, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Warren, and Washington — per the *Neighboring Counties* table on the county's [FamilySearch Wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy); an Irish Catholic couple in this era often married in the bride's parish rather than the groom's residence.
- Check the 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage and mortality schedules, found at the end of each town's population schedule, for the 12 months before each census — they record husband and wife names, ages, and marriage date and place.
- Use the 1846-1851 US Famine Irish Passenger Index and general naturalization indexes to find Thomas Hanrahan's and Johanna Ryan's arrival and naturalization, which can narrow when they were in the US and therefore when a marriage was possible.
- Identify the specific Catholic parish serving the town of Saratoga/Schuylerville circa 1855-1880 via the Diocese of Albany or the Local Catholic Church research guide before assuming any particular parish held the couple's marriage record.
- Because compliance with the 1847 and 1880 vital-records laws was incomplete, treat church records, the state censuses, and newspaper notices as primary leads rather than secondary substitutes for this specific question.
